answer_1.quote: We present a new benchmark dataset for image-text multimodal summarization... We release the resulting summaries as a dataset for multimodal summarization, called REFINE-SUMM, containing 77k article-image input pairs and corresponding summaries.
answer_1.outputs: Multimodal summaries that integrate information from both article text and associated images.

answer_2.quote: We assess the internal quality of the summaries using coherence, consistency, fluency and relevance from the UniEval framework... We also evaluate the MINT score... We employ CLIPScore... We propose its extension, Inverse TIFA (Inv-TIFA)... we also employ CLIPBERTScore to assess multimodal faithfulness.

answer_4.quote: We conduct human evaluations using Amazon Mechanical Turk to determine how informative and faithful to the source text and image (correctness) the generated summaries are... annotators provided ratings on four key dimensions: Correctness of S_i with respect to text L_i, Informativeness of S_i with respect to text L_i, Correctness of S_i with respect to image V_i, Informativeness of S_i with respect to image V_i.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators rated each summary on a 1‑4 scale for correctness and informativeness with respect to both the text and the image; pairwise preference annotations were also collected.
